description.p: Experimenting with art style a bit. Initially, I really didn't like how she turned out, but after some time has passed, I think I mellowed out a bit and I decided to post it now. Initially I wanted to draw a meme with her, but gave up on that idea half-way in. I think it's better as a standalone piece.
FYI, "Bishie" is short for "Bishōnen", which is a Japanese term for a beautiful, androgynous young guy; literally "pretty boy". All Blood Angels are twinks! 😏

I just wanted to draw some silliness again :D I'm a bit burned out from drawing serious realistic fully rendered pieces. I guess she looks too much like Grave Robber from Darkest Dungeon, but ehhh, whatever, maybe I'll draw another attempt later...

This one took me roughly two months to finish. I am somewhat satisfied, even though I struggled a lot with coloring. I really wanted to try and incorporate some style aspects from older Warhammer art, mainly from artists such as John Blanche (RIP) and Adrian Smith. I enjoyed using a very limited Zorn palette, with some cerulean blue for details. I recently re-read "A Thousand Sons" by Graham McNeill and I loved Ahriman's antics in that book. He is a like a male equivalent of a witchy tarot wine mom astrology crystals girlie... 🗿💔 Process: Sketch — Initially I wanted to somehow incorporate the city of Tizca in the background, but the composition looked off and I really didn't feel like painting urban landscape so I gave up. 💀 Alternative hairstyles — various other hairstyles I considered before settling on the final one. Warning: Some of these are goofy AF in retrospect... 🥀 Lighting and ambient occlusion layers color, texture overlays and color correction stage (final)

item.title: Deep Rock Galactic female gunner concept [artwork]

description.p: Process: sketch light source and color planning ambient occlusion painting and cleaning up; ngl, I really like how she looks here rendering overpaint layer, color correction, adjustments and effects (final, as seen above) This one was a very... Experimental piece. I was torn between painting a sassy pin-up piece vs having a more serious, "lore accurate" tone and I fear it shows. I was also trying to develop a more painterly, lineless rendering style and at least in that regard, I'd say I'm pretty happy with how it turned out. I even added some old paper and canvas textures for extra flair. I will say that I am still not 100% satisfied with it, but I managed to get it to a point where it looks alright to me and I still value it because I learned a lot from painting it. I always try to finish and "salvage" all my pieces because I think that, sometimes, you learn a lot from trying to push through the difficult part of the artwork and actually solve the problems that arise during the drawing process, instead of just giving up midway. I also think that there is still value in posting your "imperfect" art for several reasons. Firstly, we ourselves tend to be our biggest critics, so although we might not be 100% happy with our piece, it might still make someone else happy. I know a lot of artists say that they draw for themselves alone, but I personally genuinely like to share my artwork with others. Not because I need validation, although of course it's nice when people praise you, but rather, because I like to entertain others and make others feel happy with my artwork. That's the reason why I draw so many witty and humorous doodles and shitposts and fan art. Another reason is that I think we need to let go of this social media/portfolio mindset where EVERYTHING NEEDS TO BE PERFECT and you should hide all your blunders and failures and only showcase the highlights of your work. I mean, if you're making a professional portfolio — sure, but this site is NOT my portfolio and it should not be that serious. It is an ARCHIVE and that means that I want to document all of my art journey, not just the good parts.

item.title: OC: Luca von Valancious character sheet [artwork]

description.p: I will be honest, I spent something like 3+ months developing her character design and rendering her and I'm still not 100% satisfied with the final piece. The "mostly" finished piece has been sitting on my SSD for a while and yet here was just something about the piece that just felt off and unappealing to me, but I didn't know how to fix it. Still, I spent so much time and effort on it that I still wanted to showcase it, so I took out the WIP, fixed the most glaring mistakes and prettied it up to the point that I think it's "good enough". I really wanted to challenge myself with this piece and learn how to paint more realistic women and especially more masculine/androgynous physique. I definitely feel like I managed to hit my current skill ceiling and I did learn a lot about anatomy, so at least I'm happy for that part because for a while, I definitely felt like I hit a plateau in my art journey. As for the character herself, she was just a player character I envisioned when doing my first Rogue Trader playthrough. A sort of rogue-ish, asshole with a heart of gold voidborn ex-space pirate queen turned Rogue Trader by luck. I like dogmatic characters too, but I wanted a more flexible alignment for my 1st playthrough, so the crime lord background seemed more fitting. P.S. I really like the name "Luca" a lot because in my native language, "Luka" (spelled with "k") is a masculine name, while in some other languages, mainly Italian, "Luca" is a feminine name and means "light". I like it because it's unisex like that and suits this character well.
